note: Re-judged 2026-10-18 (independent auditor, after d8e084c3eb). Section 3.1: "If the resource identifier value contains a path or query component, any terminating slash (/) following the host component MUST be removed before inserting /.well-known/ and the well-known URI path suffix between the host component and the path and/or query components." The earlier wrong finding is fixed at the producer: resourceOriginAndPath (streamable_auth.go) no longer TrimRights the path; it drops only a path of "/" standing alone after the host, the slash that both follows the host and terminates the identifier's path. Read that way, RFC 8414 Section 3.1's broader "any terminating /" is narrowed by RFC 9728's "following the host component"; the reading was approved by the owner on 2026-10-18 and agrees with the Section 3.1 example. TestRFC9728TerminatingSlashRemovedBeforeInsertion: positive, https://mcp.example/ maps to .../oauth-protected-resource and https://mcp.example/?x=1 to .../oauth-protected-resource?x=1; negative, https://mcp.example/mcp/ keeps its own slash at .../oauth-protected-resource/mcp/. Each case also asserts resourceMetadataPath, the value streamable.go stores as metadataPath and ServeHTTP matches against r.URL.RequestURI(), and that no URL carries //.well-known. Restoring TrimRight reddens the /mcp/ case; losing the lone-slash removal reddens both positives.
